summary: Round 2 of LEGION-25 Part B (legion controller start, the operator-launched controller for runtime: kubernetes) on pull request #1110 at code head 40fbcb269e805acbe92b1201004098a48a313a85 (branch head a0b1dc7c = 40fbcb26 plus the implementer's handoff commit; identical code), after the reviewer's round-1 REQUEST_CHANGES on three correctness threads and the architect-authorized conflict-forced rebase onto main 73a526e3. A full round, since the fingerprint changed (d7365bb3… at my round-1 head e82da691 → bd35307d… here). The implementer's round-2 proof reproduces exactly (18/18 CLI tests, 4/4 secret-route round trips, 2/2 shipped in-cluster config files, the three real-binary refusals byte for byte). Each of the three fixes holds on its surface: the kind overlay legion.yaml resolves under --check-config and the new config.test.ts case is a real lock (restoring the overlay to its pre-fix state makes it fail with the reviewer's exact message); the docs cp operator.env line sits under the providers cp and matches the overlay's secretGenerator envs; and the real binary against a request-recording loopback listener makes zero requests when LEGION_ROLE_PROMPTS_DIR is an empty directory, when the instructions file is missing, and when it is blank, while the control run reaches the listener exactly once. The rebase moved nothing but release-managed files: the diff against main is round 1's 42-file set plus the two fix files and the three .legion handoffs; packages/pi-envoy/package.json is main's 1.36.0 with only daemonApiVersion 5 → 6; LEGION_DAEMON_API_VERSION = 6 on the branch, main still 5; claude-envoy-bridge check-dist matches a fresh build. My round-1 end-to-end re-run at the new head — the real legion controller start binary against a real in-process loopback startLegionApi with a fake omp, the /controller/ready replay, the state page under contract 6, and the Envoy-backed probe at the 240 s boundary over a loopback listener — holds in every observation, plus two new negative controls (blank dispatch_token_file, missing envoy_token_file: refused before any request). Full suites green (daemon 1669/0/14 skip, contracts 120, pi-envoy 190, tsc clean x3, biome clean); CI at 40fbcb26: Tests 34921254869 and PR Title 34921254876 success, Legion Envoy and Contracts 34921254870 success on every job. No failures. The kind check remains BLOCKED-BY-ORDER and was not run. Correction to my round-1 observation 1: ProcessManager.probeLocator throws on an unknown probe verdict and every ensureController caller catches and logs it, so an unreachable Envoy never reaches the not-registered line — the reviewer's rebuttal is right and the observation is withdrawn.

observations: Round-1 observation 1 withdrawn: ProcessManager.probeLocator (processes.ts ~2849) throws `Runtime probe reported an unknown status for the controller; ProcessManager has no unknown-status policy` on an `unknown` verdict and every ensureController caller catches and logs it, so an unreachable Envoy never reaches the not-registered line. The reviewer's rebuttal is correct; nothing to change.

After the fix the only steps between fetchControllerSecret and the spawn that can still fail locally are resolveLegionPaths (throws only for a non-absolute homeDir) and the state-directory writes (an unwritable $XDG_STATE_HOME or state_dir). Those are exactly what the reviewer's thread accepted as post-fetch (`Only writeSecretFile must follow the daemon's answer`); noting it so nobody reads the fix as making the command side-effect-free before every possible failure.
